description: The Army warned that freezing temperatures could risk an accidental toxic explosion at a munitions plant in Middletown, Iowa. description: The ingredients that go into the Hawaiian dessert guri guri – creamier than sherbet and lighter than ice cream – are a closely-guarded family secret. But on the island of Maui, where it's been served for generations, it's also a way of life. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.
title: Guri guri: A Hawaiian favorite

description: Freeze-dried and dehydrated foods have become popular with hikers for their outdoor adventures. Correspondent Conor Knighton witnesses the processes used to turn entire meals – from beef stroganoff to chicken cashew curry – into backpackable bags.
title: Just add water: Creating food for the great outdoors

description: For the award-winning star of "Monk," food had always been an integral part of family. And now he's teamed with daughter Josie Adams to write a food memoir: "We Thought They'd Never Leave," the story of their family reunions - and their recipes.
title: Tony Shalhoub on food, family, and his book, "We Thought They'd Never Leave"

description: For Emmy- and Tony-winning actor Tony Shaloub ("Monk," "The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel"), food had always been an integral part of family. And now he's teamed with daughter Josie Adams to write a food memoir: "We Thought They'd Never Leave," the story of their family, their reunions, and their recipes. They talk with correspondent Tracy Smith about the importance of breaking bread.
title: Tony Shalhoub on food and family

description: It's a fish that underwent a rebranding in the 1970s and went on to become one of the most popular seafood imports in the United States. But what is Chilean sea bass actually? Correspondent David Pogue looks into the story of a previously-unloved fish with an unfortunate name that became such a favorite of chefs and the public that it was overfished.
title: The mythic origin of Chilean sea bass

description: On a barrier island off the coast of South Carolina, Sallie Ann Robinson – chef, cookbook writer, and human whirlwind – sees food as one way to preserve Gullah Geechee culture. Correspondent Martha Teichner talks with Robinson, winner of this year's James Beard Foundation Hall of Fame Book Award.
title: Sallie Ann Robinson on preserving Gullah cuisine

description: For decades, cottage cheese was a bland, low-calorie diet food. But now social media influencers are spicing it up, adding cottage cheese to everything from pancakes to pizza crust, and demand has exploded. Correspondent David Pogue looks at how the protein craze has made a familiar dairy product … sexy.
title: How cottage cheese was made sexy

description: COP31, the latest installment of the United Nations' annual climate conference, ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed.
title: U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate

description: The New York Times named the award-winning chef's Tatiana the best restaurant in the city two years in a row. Kwame Onwuachi discusses his Afro-Caribbean menu, and his path to becoming one of today's brightest culinary stars.
title: Kwame Onwuachi's culinary journey

description: Award-winning chef Kwame Onwuachi's Tatiana, located in New York's Lincoln Center, was named the best restaurant in the city by The New York Times two years in a row. Onwuachi discusses his Afro-Caribbean menu, and his path to becoming one of today's brightest culinary stars, with correspondent Nancy Giles.
title: Kwame Onwuachi's culinary journey

description: In the rugged interior of Sardinia, a dedicated few still make a traditional form of pasta called su filindeu, or The Threads of God. Correspondent Seth Doane finds out what goes into making what is often called the rarest pasta on Earth.
title: Sardinian pasta: Making the "Threads of God"

description: In California, more than 1,300 small kitchens are licensed to make and sell food. These MEHKOs (short for "micro enterprise home kitchen operations") are run out of homes, allowing home chefs to turn family recipes into culinary passion projects.
title: Home-cooked meals, to go

description: In California, more than 1,300 small kitchens are licensed to make and sell food. These MEHKOs (short for "micro enterprise home kitchen operations") are run out of homes, allowing cooks to pursue their passions, make supplementary income, or test out potential dining concepts without the investment required for food trucks or traditional brick-and-mortar restaurants. Correspondent Luke Burbank talked with some of the home chefs who turn family recipes into culinary passion projects.
title: Home-cooked meals, to go

description: In the old days, Brussels sprouts were not exactly a favorite vegetable. But today they're a runaway hit, thanks to science.
title: How Brussels sprouts lost their bitterness

description: In the old days, Brussels sprouts were not exactly a favorite vegetable. But today they're a runaway hit, thanks to science. Correspondent David Pogue investigates what it took to make American consumption of modern Brussels sprouts nearly quintuple over the past few decades.
title: How Brussels sprouts lost their bitterness

description: Chain restaurants put a lot of America's supper clubs out of business in the 1950s and '60s, but the family-run dinner establishments continue to thrive in Wisconsin, built on Midwestern hospitality and friendliness. Correspondent Mo Rocca reports.
title: Wisconsin's supper clubs, where community is always on the menu

description: According to a recent survey, about 35% of Americans are using credit cards to buy increasingly expensive groceries – and many are having trouble paying off that food debt.

description: This Thanksgiving, Americans are paying 32% more for food compared to what we paid in 2020. But according to a recent survey, about 35% of us are using credit cards to buy groceries – and many are having trouble paying off that food debt. Correspondent Lee Cowan looks at how rising costs, and the ease of Buy Now Pay Later apps, contribute to ever-tighter food budgets.
title: Taking on credit card debt to buy food
